section_summary.extract_value: This section presents results from hierarchical multiple regression analyses examining which facets of interoceptive awareness (measured by MAIA subscales) predicted five body image variables: body appreciation, functionality appreciation, body-related pride, appearance orientation, and overweight preoccupation. The study included 646 participants (199 men, 446 women), with BMI, sex, and age entered as control variables in the first step and MAIA subscales entered in the second step. Results showed that BMI was a significant negative predictor of body appreciation, while several MAIA subscales (Attention Regulation, Self-Regulation, and Trusting) were significant positive predictors.

section_summary.extract_value: This section presents results from hierarchical multiple regression analyses examining which facets of interoceptive awareness (measured by MAIA subscales) predicted body image outcomes in a single study with N = 646 participants (199 men, 446 women). Table 2 specifically reports regression results for body appreciation and functionality appreciation as criterion variables, showing that BMI, sex, and age accounted for 12.0% and 3.7% of variance respectively, with MAIA subscales accounting for additional variance (44.0% and 29.6% respectively).
